messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=runtime-canary, check=canary-healthcheck, severity=critical — multiple 5xx responses from canary pool. Link: https://pd.redwood.example/alerts/AC-4321

pagerduty: PagerDuty event: INC-2026-4321 triggered and escalated to the on-call schedule (primary: janet-oncall). Auto-escalation in 8m if unacknowledged.

janet-oncall: ack'd. I'm on it, grabbing logs and canary dashboard.

janet-oncall: preliminary: 30% of canary pods returning 502/503 for generate_text endpoint. Latency also up ~2s. Not seeing error in infra metrics (GPU memory ok).

mike.k: I'm seeing increased error rate correlated with the new runtime sidecar introduced in today's release. Canary image tag: r-infer:v3.4.2-canary.

alex-deploy: confirmed, rollout happened at 08:12UTC. Canary fraction 5%. Only one pool (eu-west-1-a) affected.

support-liaison: Support ticket #CS-9812 came in from customer "AcmeTravel" reporting 502s for itinerary summarization — marking as potential customer impact.

ops-lead: Can we isolate traffic to previous model variant or route around canary? Any quick mitigations?

janet-oncall: Trying temporary route -> switching traffic off canary in traffic-split rule. Running:
```
redwood-ctl route update --service runtime-canary --traffic 0% --region eu-west-1
```

incident-bot: Command accepted. Traffic switch initiated. Observability: waiting 30s to validate.

mike.k: Logs from the canary pods show stacktrace in the sidecar wrapper:
```
E 2026-03-14T08:14:05Z runtime_sidecar.cpp:421 kvcache lookup failed: key_len=0
E 2026-03-14T08:14:05Z grpc::Status: INTERNAL: Unexpected empty prefix
```

janet-oncall: After routing to 0% canary, error rate in prod returned to baseline within 45s. Canary pool remains unhealthy.

ops-lead: Good. Can we mark canary as failed and trigger rollback for the canary image? What's the rollback plan?

alex-deploy: For canary we don't need full rollback since traffic already at 0, but we should abort the canary rollout and prevent promotion. I will pin stable version and block the staged rollout.

mike.k: Suggest rollback of the sidecar change in the branch and run a small repro locally. I'll open PR with revert. Reference: GH: redwood/runtime#891-revert-sidecar.

support-liaison: Notifying affected customers: CS will send initial advisory to AcmeTravel and queue follow-ups for any other anomalies in the last 10m.

ops-lead: Action items: 1) alex-deploy to block promotion and pin stable, 2) mike.k to revert PR and run regression tests, 3) janet-oncall continue monitoring and collect pod logs for postmortem, 4) support-liaison to log impacted customers.

alex-deploy: Done — promotion blocked, stable pinned. Command:
```
redwood-ctl release block --tag r-infer:v3.4.2-canary --reason "canary failures" --who alex-deploy
```

janet-oncall: Monitoring 15m window. No further pager escalations. Will hand off to next on-call in 2h for postmortem prep.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident updated: INC-2026-4321 status=acknowledged, owner=janet-oncall.

mike.k: PR opened: GH: redwood/runtime#892 revert sidecar change — running CI now.

ops-lead: After CI + validation, plan for targeted rollback to canary image and run extended canary tests before reattempt. Keep postmortem focused on sidecar KV cache handling and canary gating.

support-liaison: Logged CS-9812 as "impacted during canary window". No SLA breach yet but monitoring.

janet-oncall: Handoff: @janet-oncall -> @sylvia for next shift. I've attached pod logs and timeline to the incident ticket.

sylvia: taking follow-up, will coordinate postmortem draft.

incident-bot: Incident closed for on-call duty (no active pages). Final state: canary traffic disabled, promotion blocked, revert PR in flight.

ops-lead: Thanks all. We'll schedule blameless postmortem and add a gating test for empty-prefix KV lookups to the integration suite. :white_check_mark:
